dossier.public_summary: The dips alternate between shallow and deep at the 13.6-day period, which points to an eclipsing binary at twice that period rather than a planet. The depth also jumps dramatically between sectors and between individual transits, and a second dip near half-phase is seen. Together this is best explained by a stellar binary, likely blended with the target, not a planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by almost an order of magnitude, strong evidence for an eclipsing binary at twice the reported period (P=13.6 d vs 27.2 d), not a planet.
Depth is not consistent; per-source check shows changes_within_a_source (QLP p_constant 4.794295008265834e-11, TESS-SPOC p_constant 4.16918574341149e-25).
Signal dominated by a few very deep events; individual transits are inconsistent, characteristic of a NEB/few bad events or EB with spot activity, not a steady planetary transit.
reasons.value: 2.836877717402321e-49 / 0.967 with outliers 5812 ppm (+10.3 sigma) and 5485 ppm (+9.7 sigma)

reasons.why: Secondary-like dip at ~0.56 phase with SNR above 3 and best_brightening_snr 3.924 supports stellar companion over planet, consistent with centroid inconclusive and xgboost planet_rank 0.08.
